question: Most of Ashoka's inscriptions were in _________ language and were written in the _________ script.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Prakrit, Brahmi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Most of Ashoka's inscriptions were in the **Prakrit language**, which was the lingua franca of the time.
 
• The inscriptions were primarily written in the **Brahmi script**, which is one of the oldest writing systems used in ancient India.
 
• Ashoka's use of the Prakrit language and Brahmi script made his messages accessible to a larger audience, including the common people.
 
• These inscriptions were meant to spread the Buddhist teachings and Ashoka's policies of dharma (moral law).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prakrit Language**

 
 
• Prakrit refers to a group of Middle Indo-Aryan languages that were spoken in ancient India. It was the vernacular language of the people, in contrast to the classical Sanskrit used by the elite.
 
• Prakrits were used extensively in literature, inscriptions, and religious texts, especially in Jainism and Buddhism.
 
 
 
• **Brahmi Script**
 
 
• The Brahmi script is one of the oldest writing systems in South Asia and is the ancestor of most modern Indian scripts.
 
• It was used from the 3rd century BCE and is best known from the inscriptions of Emperor Ashoka.
 
• It is an abugida, meaning that each symbol represents a consonant with an inherent vowel, which can be changed with diacritics.
 
• The script was deciphered in the 19th century by James Prinsep, which was a significant milestone in the study of Indian epigraphy.
 
 
 
• **Ashoka's Inscriptions**
 
 
• Ashoka's inscriptions are a series of edicts on rocks and pillars that were issued by Emperor Ashoka of the Maurya Dynasty during his reign in the 3rd century BCE.
 
• These inscriptions are found across the Indian subcontinent and are written in various languages including Prakrit, Greek, and Aramaic, but Prakrit is the most common.
 
• The inscriptions serve as an important source of information about Ashoka's policies, his conversion to Buddhism, and his efforts to spread Buddhist philosophy.
 
 
 
• **Kharosthi Script**
 
 
• Kharosthi is another ancient script used in the northwestern regions of India and Central Asia, contemporary with Brahmi.
 
• It is written from right to left, unlike Brahmi which is written from left to right.
 
• While Brahmi was used for the majority of Ashoka's inscriptions, a few inscriptions in the northwest were written in Kharosthi.
